noteEntries.text:
The meeting aligned strength programming, class delivery, and premium digital training plans.

• Favor three weekly strength sessions

• Target approximately 25 participants per coach

• Plan strength blocks through the annual calendar

• Separate programming streams by training needs

• Evaluate Hyrox attendance and class capacity

• Develop TrainHeroic digital programming options

0:13
Weekly Strength-Class Schedule
Chris introduced the programming discussion and outlined the choice between two full-body sessions and three weekly strength sessions. The participants examined how the options would affect runners, existing classes, class times, and the gym’s operating model.

4:44
Preferred Three-Day Structure and Staffing
David expressed a preference for three weekly sessions, and the participants identified Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday as a workable schedule. They favored a structure that preserves access to lower-body training for runners, while coach availability remained an unresolved implementation requirement.

9:06
Annual Programming Plan
Chris presented a 12-month plan involving strength-hypertrophy training, testing, wave loading, a deload technique workshop, a December 21 endpoint, a two-week holiday closure, a four-week muscle-focused block, and a later 12-week hypertrophy block. David supported the general sequencing and recommended avoiding unnecessarily low-repetition work for the general population.

11:41
Differentiated Programming Streams
David recommended preserving heavier training options for experienced members while providing higher-volume alternatives for other participants. Chris described a potential Traineroic setup with separate programming streams, and the participants discussed whether differentiation should be based on exercises, sets and repetitions, or progression methods.

15:45
Exercise Selection and Group-Class Safety
The participants agreed that accessory work should generally use hypertrophy-oriented prescriptions, while key lifts could vary more substantially in intensity and volume. They also identified safety and coaching complexity as important considerations when prescribing demanding exercises in a large class led by one coach.

17:17
Facility Capacity and Class Flow
Chris described the rack and barbell capacity and proposed using timed working sets with accessories between them. David strongly supported a fixed clock to improve class organization, participant experience, and the coach’s ability to manage the group.

18:50
Preparation for Continued Session Design
Chris said he would review photographs of the current week’s setup to inform the next discussion. The meeting then began transitioning into the detailed structure of individual training sessions, without reaching a conclusion in the available portion.

19:12
Strength-Class Programming Structure
Chris outlined an A/B/C strength-class structure consisting of a primary compound lift, rotating lower-body accessories, and an engaging finisher. David recommended adding programming variety through formats such as AMRAPs, partner work, and hypertrophy-focused challenges.

21:01
Progression, Movement Variation, and Exercise Selection
Chris proposed maintaining the primary compound movement throughout a 10- or 12-week phase while rotating accessory movements every three to four weeks. David recommended inserting variation or deload weeks and limiting accessory volume around the primary lift to preserve coaching quality and class flow.

25:19
Deadlift Coaching and Saturday Community Sessions
Chris and David discussed whether deadlifts or RDLs should serve as primary movements and emphasized using regressions for members who struggle with deadlifting. They also characterized Saturday game days as team-based, 45-minute endurance sessions designed to build community.

30:13
ESD Programming Philosophy
Chris identified the need to understand the existing ESD goals and obtain a macro-level plan for each phase. David recommended treating ESD as year-round GPP with varied content and block-level focuses rather than attempting strict periodization based on assumptions about members’ attendance.

32:54
Programming Workload and Member Education
Chris and David agreed that high-quality ESD programming is more difficult than writing strength programs and may require access to a workout database for ideas. They estimated three to four hours per week for programming alone and discussed how structured periodization can educate members and encourage attendance.

38:42
Timetable, Attendance, and Class Demand
Chris reviewed the current timetable, including three morning ESD classes and three weekly Hyrox sessions, noting low attendance in some Hyrox time slots. David recommended evaluating whether two Hyrox sessions could meet demand, while Chris proposed formal attendance tracking to support evidence-based scheduling and resource allocation.

41:13
Capacity and Premium Positioning
The participants discussed appropriate strength-class capacity, balancing coaching quality against business growth. They leaned toward a cap in the 25-to-30 range for one coach, with additional coaches or classes added when demand warrants it, and connected the capacity decision to positioning the program as a premium offering.

43:48
Prototype Review and Delivery Plan
Chris and David reviewed a prototype training-programming interface created with Claude as an alternative to an Excel workflow. Chris plans to host it on Vercel, refine the content, add strength programming and community events, and present it to Mike and Jono the following week.

45:33
Warm-Up and Session Structure
Chris explained that warm-ups remain placeholders and described examples of current movements. David proposed a five-minute AMRAP approach to support efficient group preparation while giving the coach opportunities to engage with individual members. Chris also emphasized adding session intent, education, and guardrails, with a draft allocation of time across the session.

48:20
TrainHeroic Integration and AI Programming
Chris described using an MCP server and session token to connect the system to TrainHeroic. The process can generate draft programming for clients, which Chris reviews before publishing, provided the AI receives sufficiently clear programming guardrails.

49:50
Digital Displays and Premium Member Experience
David and Chris discussed using a polished TV display to present sessions in the gym instead of writing programs on a whiteboard. Chris proposed providing the display to all members and offering optional TrainHeroic access and exercise-demonstration videos as a paid premium feature.

52:30
Programming Progression and Revenue Model
The discussion covered programming sets, reps, RPE, percentages, and deload weeks across a training block. David recommended discussing a revenue-sharing model with Mike and Jono, while the group considered possible add-on pricing between approximately $5 and $10 per week.

56:13
Workout Resources and Follow-Up
Chris showed examples of Inertia’s aesthetic TV layouts as inspiration for the proposed system. David committed to sending a workout database, Chris planned to complete the first month for review, and both agreed to arrange another discussion the following week.
